utterances.text: Yes, comparison between the numbers -- comparative analysis of the membership of the Subnor, which is Association of Veterans Organisations of People's Liberation Struggle, Savez Udruzenja Boraca Narodnoslo bodilactcog rata, on the one hand, and the German documents concerning the enrollment of Bosnian Muslim volunteers in three particular formations, the Hanjar division, the Gendarmerie, which is not part of the SS but which was established by the plenipotentiary of the Reichsfuhrer SS Heinrich Himmler in Bosnia-Herzegovina in 1943 and the auxiliary village militia which was not part of the Ustasha militia, but was established by the Germans as a parallel body to it. The tally for the former comes to roughly 50.000 Bosnian Muslim veterans who have one way or another passed through Partizan ranks, the tally for the latter comes closer to 70.000. In fact according to one source I've seen it's 78.000. This is a very recent book published in Israel that I obtained only a few weeks ago and for which I will gladly provide reference.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I just want to make sure I understand this. It's those who are listed as members of the Veterans Association, which you named and I'm familiar with, those numbers as opposed to the numbers shown in the German records of the people that they -- and in these regiments?

utterances.speaker: SRDJA TRIFKOVIC [resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Did it ever occur to you that maybe some people didn't want to join the Veterans Association?

utterances.speaker: SRDJA TRIFKOVIC [resumed]
utterances.text: Not at all, because in the aftermath of World War II, the membership of the Veterans Association was the path to successful professional careers, jobs, and social recognition. And in fact, if anything, I believe that again on all sides of the ethnic divide, the membership was somewhat inflated because, for a good many years, it was only necessary to bring two witnesses to state that you had joined a Partizan outfit in a village or a hamlet or that you had somehow assisted the Partizans in their endeavours, and you were given recognition. This was particularly rampant not in the immediate aftermath of the war but later on in the 1950s, when it also suited the interests of the Titoist regime to even post facto inflate the ranks of the Partizans and present the movement as much more massive than it had actually been. So if anything, I would say that the published figures give, if their erroneous, they err on the size of the contingents.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Finally this, on this matter, ever occur to you that dead men can't join Veteran Associations either?

utterances.speaker: SRDJA TRIFKOVIC [resumed]
utterances.text: That is undoubtedly true. I think that the proportionate proportionality applies in that in the same way you could say that losses were incurred by the other side. What I would like to do, and this is indeed a project that I don't think has been conducted so far, is a comprehensive study of the actual losses in the former Yugoslavia during World War II. What we have at the moment is a rather tentative set of figures used by different sides for different purposes, but if we extrapolate the number of losses and if we factor in the time when different ethnic groups joined the Partizans en masse and in the case of the Croats and the Muslims, the joining en masse occurred after the collapse of Italy in September of 1943, I think that the factor of distortion would be somewhere in the region of 7 to 10 per cent and not such as to invalidate my general claim that the number of members of German supplied or German-organised units exceeded the number of volunteers joining Tito's Partizan units.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: I think we have as soon as possible to conclude, but it remains open, the question of admission into evidence the documents S409 through 413, 413 would be the article "The Hague Tribunal, Bad Justice, Worse Politics," were it wanted to go into some further details. Any objections?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, we don't have objections except for the last document and we think that it would be fair for Dr. Trifkovic to try to clarify of how many documents this one is compiled.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have no objection if Dr. Trifkovic is able to get the two articles that I agree it would be preferable.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: There were a number of questions open related to this article. Therefore, admitted into evidence the documents S409 I through S412 I. It would be for the defence to demonstrate tomorrow whether or not, and then if so, in which part, they want to tender provisional marked document D94 "The Sword of the Prophet" by Srdja Trifkovic. We have to continue tomorrow, 9.00, same courtroom, the same rules apply as in the past. The trial stays adjourned until tomorrow at 9.00.
